title: FastAPI Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Return a greeting
entries.summary: A route decorator maps GET / to a function. PlainTextResponse makes a plain text reply.

example.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, HTTPException, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
app = FastAPI()
@app.get("/", response_class=PlainTextResponse)
def hello():
    return "Hello, Asha!"

notes: Without a text response class, a returned string is sent as JSON text.

entries.name: Return a data object
entries.summary: A Python dictionary becomes JSON. Open GET /book.
notes: Return Python data instead of manually joining JSON strings.

entries.name: Check a path number
entries.summary: The n: int type lets FastAPI parse and check a route input. Open GET /double/4.
notes: Invalid input is rejected before the function body runs.

entries.name: Supply a query default
entries.summary: An input not in the path is read from the query. GET /page with no n uses its default.
notes: A default makes the query input optional.

entries.name: Limit an input range
entries.summary: Query can add rules such as a minimum and maximum. Open GET /page?n=3.
notes: Type checks alone do not enforce a useful range.

entries.name: Check a JSON body
entries.summary: A Pydantic model describes body fields. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip","pages":24}.
notes: Positive page counts need a rule such as gt=0.

entries.name: Choose returned fields
entries.summary: A response model describes the public data. GET /book leaves out the internal note.
notes: Only return data the client should receive, even when filtering is available.

entries.name: Report a missing item
entries.summary: HTTPException stops normal handling with an error reply. Open GET /missing.

example.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, HTTPException, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
app = FastAPI()
@app.get("/missing")
def missing():
    raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Book not found")

notes: Raise HTTPException; returning it is not the same action.

entries.name: Add response metadata
entries.summary: The Response input lets a function set headers. Open GET /note.
notes: A header changes metadata, not the JSON field values.

entries.name: Point to another URL
entries.summary: RedirectResponse sends a Location header. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello.
notes: Choose the redirect status deliberately, especially for non-GET methods.

entries.name: Return a typed list
entries.summary: A list response can contain several small data objects. Open GET /books.
notes: Every list item must fit the response model.

entries.name: Wait without blocking
entries.summary: An async route can await an async operation. GET /score waits for a completed coroutine and returns its result.

example.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, HTTPException, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
app = FastAPI()
async def read_score():
    return 8
@app.get("/score")
async def score():
    value = await read_score()
    return {"score": value}

notes: Do not put blocking work in async routes and assume async makes it faster.
